sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
சிந்தையெல்லாம் நிறைந்தாய் நாராயணா
முந்தை வினையும் வந்த வினையும் களைந்தே என்
sections.translit:
sindhaiyellAm niRaindhAy nArAyaNA
mundhai vinaiyum vandha vinaiyum kaLaindhE en
sections.en: Lord Narayana, you removed all of my past and present sins and have pervaded my mind.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
விந்தையே வடிவானாய் விண்ணுலகின் அரசே
எந்தையே நிகரானாய் பரிந்து தயையும் புரிந்து
sections.translit:
vindhaiyE vadivAnAy viNNulagin arasE
endhaiyE nigarAnAy parindhu dhayaiyum purindhu
sections.en: Oh, supreme Lord of the heavens, you are the personification of wonderment. You are like my father, acting with empathy and compassion and helping me each step of the way.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
கந்தை அணிந்தவன் கைபிடி அவலுக்கடிமையானாய்
நிந்தை செய்தவன் மகன் சொல் காக்க இரு உருவானாய்
பந்தை ஒத்த அளவு வெண்ணை திருடவென்றே நீயும்
மந்தை மேய்ப்பவன் போல் வந்தாய் உருகியே கண்ணீர் பெருகி நின்ற என்
sections.translit:
kandhai aNindhavan kaippidip avalukkadimaiyAnAy
nindhai seidhavan magan sol kAkka iru uruvAnAy
pandhai ottha aLavu veNNai thirudavendRE nIyum
mandhai mEyppavan pOl vandhAy urugiyE kaNNIr perugi nindRa en
sections.en: You became enamored with a fistful of flattened rice from the poor soul with tattered clothes; you transformed yourself to a half-man, half-lion form to protect the word of the young son of a fellow who constantly insulted you; you appeared as a cowherd just to steal a ball of butter. My mind softened upon hearing all these stories, and my eyes welled with tears.

notes: The charanam of this song describes three tales from Sriman Narayana’s incarnations as Narasimha and Krishna. All three episodes are detailed in the Srimad Bhagavatam. As a young boy, Krishna had a close friend named Sudama, also known as Kuchela. They received their early scriptural education together under the same teacher. During their gurukula days in Sage Sandipani’s ashram, Sudama was devoted to his divine friend. As life progressed, their paths diverged. Sudama continued his Vedic duties as a traditional Brahmin, and many times his wife urged him to visit Krishna. Knowing that Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, was Krishna’s consort, she hoped that if Sudama explained his poverty and difficult circumstances, Krishna might provide the means for them to live comfortably. Kuchela finally agreed to travel to Dwaraka to meet his old friend. He carried a small bundle of flattened rice wrapped in a cloth and slung it over his shoulder. Upon his arrival, Krishna embraced him warmly and reminisced about their school days. Sudama felt hesitant to offer the humble gift of flattened rice, but Krishna joyfully seized the bundle and ate it with delight. Sudama could not bring himself to ask Krishna for a favor. He returned home with only the memory of Krishna’s affection and hospitality. To his astonishment, his modest hut had transformed into a mansion, and his wife was adorned with gold jewelry, attended to by maids. Sudama was deeply moved by Krishna’s compassion and grace. For details, see: ஶ்ரீமத் பாகவத ஸாரம், இரண்டாம் பாகம், உரை ஆசிரியர் “அண்ணா”, ஶ்ரீ ராமகிருஷ்ண மடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 4, குசேலோபாக்கியானம், பக்கம் 255-268. For more detail about this epic friendship, see Narayaneeyam Dasakam 87. Kuchelopakyanam, Krishna’s grace The demon Hiranyakasipu performed intensive penance while chanting the name of the creator, Lord Brahma. Brahma appeared and granted him a boon that he could not be killed by a human, a beast, or a celestial, and also not be killed during the morning or night. Armed with this boon, the demon became tyrannical, attacking the celestials and proclaiming himself to be God, insisting that no one needed to worship any other deity. Hiranyakasipu had a son named Prahladha, who was born a devoted follower of Lord Vishnu. Prahladha constantly chanted the Lord’s name and spent every moment absorbed in thoughts of Him. Hiranyakasipu became enraged that he could not alter his son’s devotion and tried many times to kill him. One day, in a fit of fury, he drew his sword intending to kill Prahladha. He mockingly asked his son whether his Lord would come to save him. Striking a pillar in anger, he was shocked when Mahavishnu emerged from it in the form of Narasimha—half-lion and half-man. The divine being seized Hiranyakasipu, placed him on His thigh near a doorway at dusk, and tore open his heart with His sharp claws, thus ending the tyrant’s reign on earth. For details, see: ஶ்ரீமத் பாகவத ஸாரம், முதல் பாகம், உரை ஆசிரியர் “அண்ணா”, ஶ்ரீ ராமகிருஷ்ண மடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 4, பிரஹ்லாத சரித்திரம், பக்கம் 334-377, more specifically பக்கம் 357-361. A well-known story in the Bhagavatham is about the child Krishna stealing butter during his childhood in ஆயர்பாடி (shepherd’s village or town). As a toddler, he was very interested in playful acts such as eating sand, or drinking milk and curd. His mischievous acts, such as breaking pots to eat oozing butter is part of folklore. One such incident during his childhood in Gokulam with his mother Yasoda is described in Bhagavatham 10.9-8. For details see:ஶ்ரீமத் பாகவத ஸாரம், இரண்டாம் பாகம், உரை ஆசிரியர் “அண்ணா”, ஶ்ரீ ராமகிருஷ்ண மடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 4, கோகுல லீலை பக்கம் 3- 21, more specifically பக்கம் 10 -13.
